tweets.text:
none of these people have any kind of plan for how this would actually be effectuated 

who counts as relevant? what radius? when's the cutoff? how long to the payments run for? what defines worth? do people closer by get paid more? is the payout proportional to the nuisance? do people near DCs with onsite generation get paid more? do you get paid if you buy a house _after_ the DC is installed? do you get paid if it was an industrial site before, and that expectation was fully baked even before you bought the house? 

if the norm becomes "anyone within a 10k radius of a 250MW datacenter gets paid" people will start squatting on property or buying up land parcels nearby. it will have endless unintended and perverse consequences. 

in reality, the locals get paid already. 
- their land value likely went up, and they often have the opportunity to sell it at a massive markup to the developer 
- the DCs pay a half dozen taxes that fund city county and state, directly paying from all the services residents use 
- the residents get to file frivolous lawsuits complaining about noise which the developer will probably settle for nonzero

Yesterday, PwC came out with their long-run global AI data center spend report. My take is that their estimates dramatically understate the staying power of data center (aka the brain of AI) growth.

To put it in perspective, data center spend is still growing about 70%+ in the near term. PwC estimates annual growth between 2030 and 2050 will average 2.5%. That number feels too low. My best guess is that it probably approaches between 5–10% per year, as supported by PwC’s upside scenario of 6.5%. Those rates may look close on paper (2.5% vs. my midpoint of 7.5%), but they are not. Compounded over 20 years, 10% growth leaves annual spend about 4× what PwC’s midpoint is and about 2× their upside.

Our Deepwater Frontier Tech ETF, $LOUP, is investing in some of these data center infrastructure companies that will aim to ride the growth of AI for decades.

https://t.co/Pz3hg1cXuA

When pain comes, it's easy to get hung up in it and skip reflection. Transcendental meditation has helped me make that transition since 1969.

TM is a very simple exercise: you sit calmly and repeat a mantra in your head until all other thoughts fade away. This brings you into your subconscious mind—the space below logical awareness where emotions sit, calms you down, and where true creativity comes from.

You can’t force great ideas to come through logic, but when you relax into that subconscious space, they flow naturally.

Credit: Sam Parr, Shaan Puri, and My First Million

#TranscendentalMeditation #Mindset #RayDalio #Creativity

The application layer might make you more money... if you pick right. But picking right is hard.

Activity is concentrating on a handful of chains, and those chains are becoming the settlement layer for what comes next: billions of AI agents transacting at machine speed. You can't run that economy on banks and clearing houses that close at weekends. It'll run on the L1s.

So you don't need to guess which app breaks out. Allocate to the rails the whole machine economy will run on, size to your appetite, and let the secular trend do the work.

This is the crux of my Everything Code framework... the only things that beat the debasement of currency are the great secular trends, and this is the biggest one of all.
